newsitem.title: USA: Skipper's wrong turn cited in Maine tanker accident.
newsitem.headline: Skipper's wrong turn cited in Maine tanker accident.

text.p: Error by a docking pilot was the apparant cause of a oil tanker accident that spilled about 170,000 gallons (640,000 liters) of fuel, a federal investigator said Monday.

The pilot gave an incorrect instruction to the helmsman of the 560-foot (170-meter) tanker Julie N causing the ship to crash on Friday into a drawbridge, National Transportation Safety Board representative Bill Woody told reporters.

The accident apparently occurred as the pilot, James Mooney, a 20-year veteran of the port, was attempting to correct for tricky currents in the approach to the narrow passage through the bridge that crosses the harbor.
"The pilot freely admitted that he inadvertantly asked for a hard left when he meant a hard right," Woody told reporters.
Officials have not estimated damages from the accident, which damaged the bridge and kept the harbor partially closed to tankers and fishing boats. Cleanup operations continued on Monday.

The accident was threatening to create a potential oil shortage for Maine, and officials considered asking the Environmental Protection Agency to temporarily lift a requirement that cars in two southern counties use a special reformulated gas to reduce air pollution.
The Liberian-registered Julie N is owned by New York-based Maritime Overseas Corp, a unit of Overseas Shipholding Group Inc. a company official said. It was chartered by Global Petroleum Corp.
